title: Connection orchestration policy examples for SDK transports
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a concise, cross-language cookbook and set of runnable examples (Python, TypeScript, Go) that demonstrate practical connection orchestration patterns for the Redwood SDK transports. Patterns cover: per-route cascading timeouts (client deadline -> request slice -> single RPC), connection pool sizing and lease windows for mixed latency workloads, TCP keepalive + application-level ping strategies, adaptive idle-probe settings, and graceful streaming reconnect with partial-response retry semantics.

Background: Teams continue to misuse SDK defaults for long-polling/streaming and mixed short/long requests, which creates connection exhaustion and head-of-line latency. This ticket collects concrete recipes and sample code, aligned with runtime features (prefetch/kvcache, batching) and the Console observability fields. The deliverable is a short guide + three language folders with examples that can be copy-pasted into apps.

Scope & deliverables:
- Cookbook doc describing trade-offs and when to pick each pattern (low-latency burst vs stable throughput vs streaming recovery).
- Runnable examples: python_example.py, ts_example.mjs, go_example.go demonstrating: per-request deadline layering, keeping an idle connection warm without preventing pool rebalancing, and best practice for reconnecting streaming responses with resumed KV-cache offsets.
- Test harness (smoke) that simulates mixed workload: 90% short (50-200ms), 10% long streaming (10s) to validate pool behaviour.
- PR with README and unit + integration smoke tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Examples run locally and produce metrics (latency, connection_count) that match expected patterns documented in the cookbook.
- Observability: sample traces show per-request deadline propagation and pool lease durations.
- Cross-code reviewers (SDK lead for each language) approve ergonomics and error surface.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive keepalive prevents unnecessary reconnect but ties up sockets; recommend short keepalive with small standby pool + idle_probe to maintain cold-start cost.
- Long per-socket leases simplify streaming but reduce headroom for bursts; propose configurable per-route lease windows.

Planned code highlights (included in examples):
- Python: requests use layered deadlines (contextlib + timeout wrapper). Example shows adapt_timeout = min(client_deadline, route_slo) and per-connection keepalive=30s with pool_min=2 pool_max=20.
- TypeScript: AbortController-based per-call deadlines with fetch-like transport hooks and a keepalive ping loop that backs off exponentially when pool pressure increases.
- Go: context.Context deadlines per RPC and net.Dialer KeepAlive with a connection supervisor (goroutine) that prunes idle sockets after N miss-pings.

Longer term: recommendations will feed into default SDK transport presets (follow-up ENG ticket to land defaults once validated).
